spec.name: UTF-8 prefix candidate
requirements: Repair the Python function truncate_utf8(text, byte_limit). Return the longest starting prefix of text whose UTF-8 encoding is at most byte_limit bytes. Preserve the original characters and order exactly, including whitespace and control characters. Never normalize, replace, transliterate, skip characters, or split a Unicode code point. The host supplies a Unicode scalar-value string of at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes and an integer byte_limit from 0 through 4096; booleans and unpaired surrogates are excluded. A zero budget returns an empty string, and a budget larger than the whole encoding returns the original string. Boundaries are Unicode code points, not grapheme clusters: combining marks, emoji modifiers, regional indicators, and ZWJ sequences may be separated at code-point boundaries. Define truncate_utf8(text, byte_limit) and return only its string result; the host handles JSON input an

d output. You may revise the candidate at most twice using development feedback. The held-out suite is unavailable during revision. This is a candidate-only code-repair warm-up, not a native source repair, weight-training result, or production activation.
